problem: Refine imitation policies using imagined rollouts without collecting additional physical interactions during the refinement stage.
contribution: World4RL combines an EDM diffusion transition model, two-hot continuous-action conditioning, learned success classifier and PPO. Training data deliberately include expert, policy and random behavior to cover failures; offline refinement is distinct from initial data collection.
algorithm: Pretrain BC policy and330M U-Net transition model on finite observation/action histories; map each action to nearest-bin interpolation weights (21bins example). ResNet18 reward classifier trains on success-labeled examples. Freeze learned environment and run PPO in generated observations; cap policy standard deviation to reduce OOD model exploitation. Ablate action representations and random-rollout coverage.
observations: Visual context of four frames and aligned continuous actions; task-specific success labels. Initial physical observation begins autoregressive simulation. Learned visual success probability is not force sensing or a proof of correct contact dynamics.
actions: Task-specific continuous controls with two-hot encoding and Gaussian policy. Encoding preserves interpolation within declared bins but does not align different embodiments or justify extrapolation beyond support.
embodiment_and_data: Six Meta-World tasks, each50expert+150BC+30random trajectories of50steps. Real FrankaPanda tasks each50expert+50policy+50random trajectories;20 physical trials/task with fixed scene/start pose. World-model pretraining4 A80040GB GPUs20h; refinement one A800~6h/task.
experiments: Video FVD/FID/LPIPS; simulated sparse-success policy comparison over3seeds; six real tasks versus BC/DP; variance-cap and random-data ablations. Offline TD-MPC2 is adapted to fixed-data setting, differing from its standard online formulation. Data counts differ across imitation/offline-RL/world-model baselines.
baselines: BC/DP on50expert demonstrations;TD3+BC/IQL onexpert+policy data;IRASim/DiWA/adapted TD-MPC2 on230trajectories;Uni-O4/RLPD additionally collect online interactions. Keep these budgets visible when citing efficiency.
quantitative_result: TableII PDFp6:Meta-World average67.5% versusBC51.5%,TD3+BC57.7%,TD-MPC2offline60.0%. TableIIIp7 physical20trials/task:average93.3% versusDP88.3%; the table prints BC68.3%, but its listed task counts sum to72/120=60.0%, an unresolved internal inconsistency; negative case put-bread-in16/20 versusDP18/20 retained. Fixed initial scene/pose limits generalization. Fig3 sample-efficiency bars omit30random trajectories despite world-model training description; do not quote10k as complete collection cost.
limitations: Learned-model OOD behavior remains fragile; action variance cap and broad training coverage are important. Real tests use fixed starts and small denominators. Moderate image resolution/model capacity and reward-classifier bias constrain reliability. Video-quality gains are not equivalent to verified physical accuracy. TableIII BC average conflicts with its six raw trial counts; retain both and prefer raw counts for independent recomputation.

Physical SO101/ROSMASTER adaptation needs calibrated action bounds, outcome labels and measured runtime; current controller settings stay unchanged.
